draftNote: Read from one blockprint at the resolution of an online scan; doubtful places are marked in the notes, and the text has not yet been collated with other prints.
source: Zab chos zhi khro dgongs pa rang grol las: Chos nyid bar do'i gsal 'debs thos grol chen mo, pages 36–45 of the reproduction, from an undated Tibetan blockprint of the Thos grol cycle reproduced by the Buddhist Digital Resource Center as W23710 (text kha), read from the page images. It is a traditional blockprint, so no modern editor's work is involved. Two transcriptions found online, one of this print and one of another, were used to check the reading and are not the text. The page gives the print's wording and spelling. Three things are ours: the spaces between words, which Tibetan does not write; the line-end abbreviations, written out; and clear misprints corrected, each named in its note. Where another print reads differently in a way that matters, the note says so. Letters: the Wylie system (Extended Wylie for the Sanskrit words). Pronunciation: the reading style of central Tibet in the THL Simplified Phonetic Transcription (Germano and Tournadre, 2003), produced by rule from the spelling; a living reader's pronunciation will differ in places. The translation is new, made from the Tibetan. Still to do: the text has been read from one print at the resolution of an online scan, and doubtful places are marked in the notes; it has not been collated with the other blockprints.

sentences.l: Then, the Blessed-One Vairocana father-mother('s), you, the between's narrow-passage in, meeting for come it-is.
sentences.i: Then the Blessed One Vairocana and his consort have come to meet you in the narrow passage of the bardo.
sentences.n: The first words, de nas bcom ldan, stand at the end of p. 35, after the last sentence of the part before. 'phrang is a narrow passage, a defile on a mountain road where the traveller is at the mercy of whatever meets him; the bardo is spoken of as one. bsu ba, 'to go out to meet, to welcome', is the word for receiving a guest on the road; bsu ba la 'ongs pa, 'has come to meet'. 'ongs is the past of 'ong, 'to come'. yab yum gyi has the ending 'of' where the subject stands (the other recension has the same); it is read as marking the subject, as gyis would, and the translation passes over it.

sentences.l: That, you by, delusion fierce accumulated's habitual-tendencies' welcomer's path it-is.
sentences.i: That is the path on which the habitual tendencies of the fierce delusion you have gathered come out to meet you.
sentences.n: gti mug, 'delusion, bewilderment', the not-seeing that is one of the poisons of the mind, the poison of the first day; each day's dull light answers to one of them, and this one leads to the gods. bsags, 'gathered, accumulated', past of gsog: khyod kyis ... bsags pa'i, 'which you have gathered', is a clause before its noun, closed by -pa'i. bsu ma'i lam, 'the path of the welcomer': the dull light, too, comes out to receive him, as the buddhas do. In the same sentence on the second day the print has bsu ba'i lam, 'the path of welcoming'.

sentences.l:
Alas! Delusion fierce-by in-saṃsāra wandering's time,
the dharma-expanse wisdom bright's light-path on,
the Blessed-One Vairocana the-way lead!
The mother supreme Expanse-Lady by from-behind support!
The between fearful's narrow-passage from freeing I-pray;
the genuine perfect buddha's level-to bring!
sentences.i:
Alas! When I wander in saṃsāra through fierce delusion,
on the bright light-path of the wisdom of the expanse of reality
may the Blessed One Vairocana lead the way,
may the supreme mother, Lady of the Expanse, support me from behind.
I pray you, free me from the fearful narrow passage of the bardo
and bring me to the level of a true and perfect buddha.
sentences.n: Verse: six lines of nine syllables (the first with kyai ma before it, the same cry as kye ma), the prayer the dead person says after the reader. It comes back on each day with that day's poison, wisdom, buddha and consort. chos dbyings is chos kyi dbyings, 'the expanse of reality', shortened for the metre; its wisdom is Vairocana's. 'od lam, 'light-path': the light is the road. lam sna, 'the head of the road'; drongs is the imperative of 'dren, 'to lead': lam sna drongs, 'go before and lead the way'. rgyab nas skyor, 'hold up from behind'. yis is the 'by' ending after a vowel, used in verse. Dbyings phyug ma, 'Lady of the Expanse', is Nam mkha'i dbyings phyug ma of the last part, shortened. bsgral du gsol, 'I pray that you free': bsgral, the future stem of sgrol, 'to free, to deliver', with du gsol, 'I ask that'. yang dag rdzogs pa'i sangs rgyas, 'the truly and perfectly awakened one', is a fixed title of a buddha (Sanskrit samyaksaṃbuddha); sa, 'ground, level', the stage reached; skyol, 'bring, deliver', the imperative of skyel. 'khyams ba'i is the print's spelling of 'khyams pa'i.

sentences.l: So-saying, devotion-respect fierce-by, prayer thus made-because: Vairocana's heart-in as-rainbow-light dissolving, then, the centre-direction, Densely-Arrayed's realm-in, as-the-body-of-perfect-enjoyment buddha becomes.
sentences.i: When he makes this prayer with fierce devotion, he dissolves as rainbow light into the heart of Vairocana and becomes a buddha in the body of perfect enjoyment in the central realm, the Densely Arrayed.
sentences.n: zhes, 'thus', closes the quoted prayer. mos gus, 'devotion and respect'. btab pas, 'because ... made': btab is the past of 'debs, the verb for making a prayer. 'ja' 'od, 'rainbow light'; thim, 'to dissolve, to be absorbed'. Stug po bkod pa, 'Densely Arrayed' (stug po, 'thick, dense'; bkod pa, 'arranged, set out'), is here the name of the buddha-field of the centre, rendered word by word; the last part named the central realm from which Vairocana comes Thig le brdal ba, the Spreading Drop. longs spyod rdzogs pa'i sku, 'the body of perfect enjoyment', is the radiant form in which buddhas appear in visions, the second of the three bodies of the pilot's opening verse. sangs rgyas par 'gyur ro, 'becomes a buddha'. Where the print has de skad du, 'thus', and Vairocana's heart, the other recension has neither 'thus' nor the print's single buddha: it has the heart of Vairocana and his consort.

sentences.n: The print has ཞི་སྡང, a misprint for ཞེ་སྡང, 'anger', corrected here: zhi is 'peace', the print writes zhe sdang everywhere else on these pages, and the other recension has zhe sdang here. The print also has བཀྲག, 'lustre', a misprint for སྐྲག, 'frightened', corrected here: it is the same swap of skrag and bkrag as in the last part, and the other recension has skrag. zhe sdang, 'anger, hatred', is the poison of the second day. sdig sgrib, 'sin-obscuration', the veil left on the mind by harmful deeds. rkyen, 'condition, circumstance'; rkyen gyis, 'through the force of'. na yang, 'even if'. sentences.n: byang chub sems dpa', 'awakening-hero' (Sanskrit bodhisattva), one who has vowed to become a buddha for the sake of others. Sa'i snying po, 'Essence of the Earth' (Kṣitigarbha); Byams pa, 'the Loving One' (Maitreya), with the Sanskrit maitri after it in Tibetan letters, me tri. sems ma is short for sems dpa' ma, 'female bodhisattva'. Lāsyā, 'she of the dance', and Puṣpā, 'she of flowers', are Sanskrit names in Tibetan letters; the print spells the first ལཱ་སྱ་མ where the other recension has ལཱ་སྱེ་མ. la after the first pair is read as joining it to the second: the four together surround the buddha and his consort, and the six are these. bskor, 'surrounded'. klung is the print's spelling here of klong, 'expanse', which it writes klong on the third day; klung as a word by itself is 'river'. 'char nas 'ong ngo, 'they come dawning'. The other recension has 'ja' dang 'od dang zer, 'rainbow, light and rays'.

sentences.l:
Alas! Anger fierce-by in-saṃsāra wandering's time,
the mirror wisdom bright's light-path on,
the Blessed-One Vajrasattva-by the-way lead!
The mother supreme Buddha-Eye-by from-behind support!
The between fearful's narrow-passage(?) from freeing I-pray;
the genuine perfect buddha's level-to bring!
sentences.i:
Alas! When I wander in saṃsāra through fierce anger,
on the bright light-path of the mirror-like wisdom
may the Blessed One Vajrasattva lead the way,
may the supreme mother Buddhalocanā support me from behind.
I pray you, free me from the fearful narrow passage of the bardo
and bring me to the level of a true and perfect buddha.
sentences.n: The curled mark ༈ opens the prayer as a section. It is the verse of the first day with the second day's poison, wisdom, buddha and consort. Here both buddha and consort carry -s, 'by' (rdo rje sems dpas, sangs rgyas spyan mas), as the first day's consort carried yis. me long ye shes is me long lta bu'i ye shes, shortened for the metre. bskyor, the past and future stem of skyor, 'hold up', stands where the first day has skyor; the prayer asks, so the sense is 'hold up!' as there. The last letter of 'phrang in the fifth line cannot be told on the image from the ད of 'phrad, 'meeting', so the reading is uncertain; 'phrang is taken because the line is the same as on the first day.

sentences.l: The bodhisattva Sky's-Essence and All-Good, two, with; the female-bodhisattvas Mālyā and Dhūpā, two, by surrounded, then; rainbow and light's expanse from, buddha's(?) bodies six-as dawning come.
sentences.i: Surrounded by the two bodhisattvas Ākāśagarbha and Samantabhadra and the two female bodhisattvas Mālyā and Dhūpā, they come, dawning as six buddha forms out of an expanse of rainbow and light.
sentences.n: Nam mkha'i snying po, 'Essence of Space' (Ākāśagarbha). Kun tu bzang po, 'the All-Good' (Samantabhadra), is here the bodhisattva of that name, not the primordial buddha of 002. Mālyā, 'she of the garland', and Dhūpā, 'she of incense', are Sanskrit names in Tibetan letters, spelled by the print mA l+yam and dhu pe ma (the other recension has mA le ma). The print writes nam mkha'i contracted (ནམཁའི); it is written out. sangs rgyas kyis has the ending 'by' where kyi, 'of', is meant; the print is kept and read so. As on the second day, the other recension adds zer, 'rays', to the rainbow and light.

sentences.l: Feeling's aggregate in-the-expanse pure: light yellow, sameness's wisdom, yellow and shimmering, drops and small-drops by adorned, bright and clear, eye by to-look not bearable, one,
sentences.i: The aggregate of feeling, pure in the expanse, is the yellow light, the wisdom of sameness: yellow and shimmering, adorned with drops and smaller drops, bright and clear, too bright for the eye to look at.
sentences.n: tshor ba, 'feeling', the second aggregate: the sense of things as pleasant, painful or neither. dbyings su dag ba, 'pure in the expanse', where the days before had gnas su, 'in its place'; dag ba is the print's spelling of dag pa. mnyam pa nyid, 'sameness' (mnyam, 'equal'; nyid, '-ness'); its wisdom (Sanskrit samatājñāna) sees all things as equal. thig le, 'drop, sphere', and thig phran, 'small drop': points of light within the light. brgyan, 'adorned'. mtsher is read as 'tsher, as before. blta mi bzod pa, 'unbearable to look at'.

sentences.l: That's state in, knowing nothing-to-do's state in, loosen, and, rest!
sentences.i: Within it, relax and rest in the state of awareness where there is nothing to do.
sentences.n: ngang, 'state, natural condition'. byar med, 'nothing to be done' (bya, 'to do', with -r, and med, 'there is not'): awareness left as it is, without effort. glod, 'to loosen, to relax'. bzhogs shig, 'rest!, leave it!', is not the usual form: the imperative of 'jog, 'to place, to leave', is zhog, which the other recension has (lhod la zhog cig, 'relax and leave it'). sentences.l: You-yourself's knowing's own-radiance-as face know if, as-for: devotion-respect not done, prayer not made though, bodies and light-rays all, you-yourself with inseparable-as dissolving, then, buddha become.
sentences.i: If you recognise it as the natural radiance of your own awareness, then even without devotion and without making the prayer, all the forms and lights dissolve into you, inseparable from you, and you become a buddha.
sentences.n: rang mdangs, 'own radiance', the glow of awareness itself. ma byas, ma btab, 'not done, not made', past forms with ma. dbyer med du, 'inseparably, without being apart': the forms and lights and the one who sees them become one. The part ends here; the print line goes on with the other case, rang gi rig pa'i rang mdangs su ma shes na ni, 'if you do not recognise it ...', which begins the next part.

glossary.དེ་ལྟར་དུ: de ltar du — in that way, thus (de ltar 'thus' + -du)
glossary.དེ་སྐད་དུ: de skad du — thus, in these words (de 'that' + skad 'speech, words' + -du 'in')
glossary.དྲག་པོ: drag po — fierce, strong, violent (drag po)
glossary.དྲག་པོས: drag pos — by the fierce, by the strong (drag po 'fierce' + -s 'by')
glossary.དྲུག་ཏུ: drug tu — among six, as six (drug 'six' + -tu 'among, as'): rigs drug tu 'among the six kinds'; sku drug tu 'as six bodies'
glossary.དྷུ་པེ་མ: dhu pe ma — Dhūpā, 'she of incense' (dhu pe, for Sanskrit dhūpe, the name in the form used in addressing her, from dhūpa 'incense', + -ma, feminine): a female bodhisattva
glossary.ན: na — if, when (after the verb); also 'in, at'
glossary.ནམ་མཁའི་སྙིང་པོ: nam mkha'i snying po — Essence of Space (nam mkha' 'sky, space' + -'i + snying po 'essence'; Sanskrit Ākāśagarbha): a bodhisattva
glossary.ནས: nas — from; after a verb: 'having done, and then'
glossary.ནི: ni — as for: marks the topic of the sentence
glossary.པུཥྤེ་མ: puShpe ma — Puṣpā, 'she of flowers' (puṣpe, the Sanskrit name in the form used in addressing her, from puṣpa 'flower', + -ma, feminine): a female bodhisattva
glossary.ཕུང་པོ: phung po — mass, heap (phung po) · aggregate, one of the five that make up a person (phung po; Sanskrit skandha)
glossary.ཕྱག: phyag — hand (phyag), the respectful word; also 'homage'
glossary.བཀྲག་མདངས: bkrag mdangs — lustre and radiance (bkrag 'lustre' + mdangs 'glow')
glossary.བཀྲག་མདངས་ཅན: bkrag mdangs can — having lustre and radiance, lustrous and radiant (bkrag 'lustre' + mdangs 'glow' + can 'having')
glossary.བག་ཆགས: bag chags — habitual tendencies, the traces past actions leave in the mind (bag chags; Sanskrit vāsanā)
glossary.བཅོམ་ལྡན: bcom ldan — Blessed One, a title of a buddha (bcom ldan, short for bcom ldan 'das)
glossary.བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས: bcom ldan 'das — the Blessed One, a title of a buddha (bcom ldan 'das, Sanskrit bhagavān; 'das 'gone beyond')
glossary.བཏབ་པས: btab pas — by having given, because it is given (btab pa + -s 'by')
glossary.བཞུགས་པ: bzhugs pa — abiding, being present (bzhugs, respectful 'stay' + -pa)
glossary.བཞོགས་ཤིག: bzhogs shig — rest! leave it! (bzhogs + shig, which marks a command; perhaps the print's form for zhog, imperative of 'jog 'place, leave')
glossary.བཟོད་པ: bzod pa — bearing, endurance (bzod 'bear, endure' + -pa): mi bzod pa 'unbearable'
glossary.བཟོད་པའི: bzod pa'i — of bearing, that can be borne (bzod pa 'bearing' + -'i 'of'): mi bzod pa'i 'unbearable'
glossary.བར་ཆད: bar chad — obstacle, hindrance, interruption (bar chad)
glossary.བར་དོ: bar do — the between: the interval between two states, above all between death and rebirth (bar 'between' + do 'two')
glossary.བར་དོའི: bar do'i — of the bardo (bar do + -'i 'of')
glossary.བརྒྱན་པ: brgyan pa — adorned, decorated (brgyan, past of rgyan 'to adorn', + -pa)
glossary.བལྟ: blta — to look (blta, future stem of lta 'look'): blta mi bzod pa 'unbearable to look at'
glossary.བལྟ་བར: blta bar — in looking, looking (blta, future stem of lta 'look', + -bar): mig ma blta bar 'without looking with the eye'
glossary.བསགས་པའི: bsags pa'i — of what is gathered, which has been gathered (bsags 'gather, pile up', past of gsog, + -pa'i 'of'): a clause placed before its noun
glossary.བསུ་བ: bsu ba — meeting, welcoming, going out to meet someone (bsu 'to meet, welcome' + -ba); bsu ba la 'ongs 'come to meet'
glossary.བསུ་བའི: bsu ba'i — of welcoming, of meeting (bsu ba 'welcoming' + -'i 'of')
glossary.བསུ་མའི: bsu ma'i — of welcoming, of the welcomer (bsu 'to meet, welcome' + -ma, which makes a noun, perhaps 'the one who welcomes', + -'i 'of'); beside bsu ba'i in the same phrase
glossary.བསྐོར: bskor — surrounded, encircled (bskor, past of skor 'to surround, to circle')
glossary.བསྐྱོར: bskyor — held up, to hold up, support (bskyor, past and future stem of skyor 'hold up'); in a request, perhaps standing for 'hold up!'
glossary.བསྒྲལ་དུ: bsgral du — to free, to deliver (bsgral, future stem of sgrol 'to free', + -du): bsgral du gsol 'I pray that you free'
glossary.བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ: byang chub sems dpa' — bodhisattva (byang chub 'awakening' + sems dpa' 'hero of mind')
glossary.བྱམས་པ་མེ་ཏྲི: byams pa me tri — Maitreya, the Loving One (byams pa 'loving' + me tri, Sanskrit maitri in Tibetan letters): a bodhisattva
glossary.བྱར་མེད: byar med — with nothing to do, effortless (bya, future stem of byed 'do', 'to be done', + -r + med 'there is not')
glossary.བྱས: byas — did, made, having done (byas, past of byed 'do')
glossary.བྱེད་ཅིག: byed cig — do (byed, the present stem of byed 'do', + cig, which marks a command): with ma, a prohibition, ma byed cig 'do not do!' (the imperative of byed is gyis)
glossary.བྲོས: bros — fled, ran away (bros, past of 'bros 'flee')
glossary.བྲོས་པས: bros pas — because it has fled (bros pa, past of 'bros 'run away', + -s)
glossary.བྲོས་སུ: bros su — fleeing, in flight (bros, past of 'bros 'to flee', + -su): bros su 'ong 'will flee'
glossary.མ: ma — not (before past and imperative verbs) · in a prohibition also before the present stem: ma byed cig 'do not do!'
glossary.མངོན་པར་དགའ་བའི: mngon par dga' ba'i — of Manifest Joy (mngon par 'manifestly' + dga' ba 'joy' + -'i 'of'; Sanskrit Abhirati): the buddha-field of the east
glossary.མངོན་བར་དགའ་བའི: mngon bar dga' ba'i — of Manifest Joy (mngon bar, the print's spelling of mngon par 'manifestly', + dga' ba 'joy' + -'i 'of')
glossary.མཆིའོ: mchi'o — I go (mchi, the humble 'go', + the sentence-ending -'o)
glossary.མཉམ་དུ: mnyam du — together, along with (mnyam 'equal, same' + -du)
glossary.མཉམ་པ་ཉིད: mnyam pa nyid — sameness, equality (mnyam pa 'equal' + nyid '-ness')
glossary.མཐིང་ཁ: mthing kha — deep blue (mthing kha, the print's spelling of mthing ga)
glossary.མདུན་དུ: mdun du — in front (mdun 'the front' + du)
glossary.མཚེར་བ: mtsher ba — shimmering (the print's spelling, read as 'tsher ba; mtsher is no known word)
glossary.མཱ་མ་ཀི: mā ma ki — Māmakī, 'She Who Is Mine': a Sanskrit name in Tibetan letters, the consort of the south
glossary.མཱ་ལྱམ: mā lyam — Mālyā, 'she of the garland' (mā lyam, the print's letters for a Sanskrit name from mālya 'garland'; the other recension has mā le ma): a female bodhisattva
glossary.མི: mi — not (before present and future verbs)
glossary.མི་བསྐྱོད་པ: mi bskyod pa — the Unshakeable (mi 'not' + bskyod 'move, shake' + -pa; Sanskrit Akṣobhya): the buddha of the east
glossary.མིའི: mi'i — of humans, of a human (mi 'human' + -'i 'of')
glossary.མོས་གུས: mos gus — devotion and respect (mos 'devotion' + gus 'respect')
glossary.མོས་པ: mos pa — devotion, trust, interest (mos pa)
glossary.ཙམ་དུ: tsam du — just so far, just to the point of (tsam + du)
glossary.ཚུད: tshud — to get into, to be caught in, to sink into (tshud)
glossary.ཚེ་འདས: tshe 'das — one whose life has passed, the dead person (tshe 'life' + 'das 'gone beyond')
glossary.ཚོར་བའི: tshor ba'i — of feeling (tshor ba 'feeling' + -'i 'of'): feeling is the second of the five aggregates
glossary.ཞག: zhag — day, a day and night (zhag)
glossary.ཞལ་སྦྱར: zhal sbyar — in union, face joined to face (zhal 'face', respectful, + sbyar 'joined')
glossary.ཞིང་ཁམས་སུ: zhing khams su — in the realm, in the buddha-field (zhing khams 'realm' + -su 'in')
glossary.ཞེ་སྡང: zhe sdang — anger, hatred (zhe sdang), the mind's poison of the second day
glossary.ཞེན་ཅིག: zhen cig — cling! (zhen 'cling' + cig, which marks a command); ma zhen cig 'do not cling'
glossary.ཞེས: zhes — so, thus: closes a quotation or a name (like inverted commas)
glossary.ཟུག: zug — to pierce, to stab, to stick in (zug)
glossary.ཟེར: zer — say, call (zer 'say, speak') · ray, ray of light (zer), as in 'od zer, and sgra 'od zer gsum 'sound, light and rays'
glossary.འཁོར་བར: 'khor bar — in saṃsāra, in the round ('khor ba 'the round, saṃsāra' + -r 'in')
glossary.འཁྱམས་པའི: 'khyams pa'i — of wandering, when one wanders ('khyams 'wander' + -pa'i 'of')
glossary.འཁྱམས་བའི: 'khyams ba'i — of wandering, when one wanders ('khyams 'wander' + -ba'i 'of', the print's spelling of -pa'i)
glossary.འགྱུར་རོ: 'gyur ro — becomes, will become ('gyur 'to become, to change' + the sentence-ending -ro)
glossary.འཆར: 'char — to dawn, to arise, to appear
glossary.འཇའ་འོད་དུ: 'ja' 'od du — as rainbow light, into rainbow light ('ja' 'rainbow' + 'od 'light' + -du 'as, into')
glossary.འཇིགས: 'jigs — to fear, to be afraid ('jigs); fear
glossary.འཇིགས་པའི: 'jigs pa'i — of fear, fearful, terrifying ('jigs pa 'fear' + -'i 'of')
glossary.འཇིགས་པར: 'jigs par — in fear, afraid ('jigs pa 'fear' + -r): ma 'jigs par 'without fear, not fearing'
glossary.འདམ་དུ: 'dam du — into mud, into a mire ('dam 'mud, mire' + -du 'into')
glossary.འདི་སྐད་དུ: 'di skad du — in these words, thus ('di 'this' + skad 'speech, words' + -du 'in')
glossary.འདི་སྐད་དོ: 'di skad do — these words (are said) ('di 'this' + skad 'speech' + the sentence-ending -do)
glossary.འདུ་ཤེས: 'du shes — notion, perception, idea ('du shes; Sanskrit saṃjñā)
glossary.འཕྲང: 'phrang — narrow passage, defile, a dangerous place on a road ('phrang)
glossary.འབྱུང: 'byung — to come about, to occur, to arise ('byung; byung is its past)
glossary.འབྱུང་བ: 'byung ba — element, one of the five of which the world is made: earth, water, fire, wind, space ('byung ba, literally 'what arises') · arising, coming about ('byung 'arise' + -ba)
glossary.འོང: 'ong — comes, happens, it may happen that ('ong 'come')
glossary.འོངས་པ: 'ongs pa — come, having come ('ongs, past of 'ong 'come', + -pa)
glossary.འོད་ཟེར: 'od zer — ray of light, radiance ('od 'light' + zer 'ray')
glossary.འོད་ལམ: 'od lam — light-path, path of light ('od 'light' + lam 'path')
glossary.ཡང: yang — also, even, though (written kyang after g, d, b, s) · again, once more, at the head of a sentence (yang ngo sprad pa ni 'and the pointing out again')
glossary.ཡང་དག: yang dag — true, genuine, perfect (yang dag): yang dag rdzogs pa'i sangs rgyas 'true and perfect buddha' (Sanskrit samyaksaṃbuddha)
glossary.ཡང་ན: yang na — or else, or (yang na)
glossary.ཡབ་ཡུམ: yab yum — father and mother; a buddha and his consort in union (yab 'father' + yum 'mother')
glossary.ཡིན་ནོ: yin no — is, are (yin 'to be' + the sentence-ending -no)
glossary.ཡིས: yis — by (the 'by' ending after a vowel, used in verse; yis)
glossary.ཡུམ: yum — mother; a buddha's female partner, consort (yum)
glossary.ཡེ་ཤེས: ye shes — wisdom, primordial knowing (ye 'from the first' + shes 'know'; Sanskrit jñāna)
glossary.ཡེ་ཤེས་སུ: ye shes su — as wisdom (ye shes 'wisdom' + -su 'as'): ye shes su ngo shes 'recognise as wisdom'
glossary.ཡེངས་པར: yengs par — distractedly, in distraction (yengs pa 'to be distracted' + -r): ma yengs par 'undistracted'
glossary.ཡོངས་པ: yongs pa — uncertain: perhaps 'come', read as 'ongs pa; yongs by itself means 'all, entire', which does not fit here
glossary.རང་མདངས་སུ: rang mdangs su — as one's own radiance (rang 'own' + mdangs 'glow' + -su 'as')
glossary.རིག་པ: rig pa — knowing, awareness itself, before any thought
glossary.རིག་པའི: rig pa'i — of knowing, of awareness (rig pa 'knowing' + -'i 'of')
glossary.རིགས་ཀྱི་བུ: rigs kyi bu — child of the family, child of noble family (rigs 'family' + kyi 'of' + bu 'son, child'; Sanskrit kulaputra)
glossary.རིན་ཆེན་འབྱུང་ལྡན: rin chen 'byung ldan — Source of Jewels (rin chen 'jewel, precious thing' + 'byung ldan 'having arising'; Sanskrit Ratnasambhava): the buddha of the south and of the third day
glossary.རིན་པོ་ཆེ: rin po che — precious, a precious thing, jewel (rin 'value' + po + che 'great')
glossary.རྐྱེན: rkyen — condition, circumstance, cause (rkyen): rkyen gyis 'through the force of'
glossary.རྒྱབ: rgyab — back, behind (rgyab): rgyab nas 'from behind'
glossary.རྡོ་རྗེ: rdo rje — vajra, the diamond-thunderbolt held by deities, emblem of what cannot be broken (rdo rje)
glossary.རྡོ་རྗེ་སེམས་དཔའ: rdo rje sems dpa' — Vajrasattva, 'Vajra Being' (rdo rje 'vajra' + sems dpa' 'hero of mind'; Sanskrit vajrasattva): the buddha of the second day, here the same figure as Akṣobhya
glossary.རྡོ་རྗེ་སེམས་དཔའི: rdo rje sems dpa'i — of Vajrasattva (rdo rje sems dpa' + -'i 'of'): the buddha of the second day
glossary.རྡོ་རྗེ་སེམས་དཔས: rdo rje sems dpas — by Vajrasattva (rdo rje sems dpa' + -s 'by')
glossary.རྣམ་པར: rnam par — completely, in every way (rnam par): rnam par dag pa 'completely pure'
glossary.རྣམ་པར་སྣང་མཛད: rnam par snang mdzad — Vairocana, 'He Who Makes Appear in Every Way' (rnam par 'in every way' + snang 'appear' + mdzad, respectful 'do, make'); the buddha of the centre
glossary.རྩེ་ལྔ་པ: rtse lnga pa — five-pointed (rtse 'point, tip' + lnga 'five' + -pa)
glossary.རྫོགས་པའི: rdzogs pa'i — of the perfect, complete (rdzogs pa 'perfect' + -'i 'of')
glossary.ལ: la — to, at, in, for; after a verb or adjective: 'and'
glossary.ལ་ལ: la la — some, certain ones (la la)
glossary.ལད་མོ: lad mo — imitation, copying (lad mo): lad mo byed 'repeat after someone'
glossary.ལམ་སྣ: lam sna — head of the road, the way ahead (lam 'path' + sna 'front, head'): lam sna drongs 'lead the way'
glossary.ལས: las — from, out of · karma, action (las): las kyi 'of karma'; after a verb or noun, 'other than, of, from among'
glossary.ལས་ངན: las ngan — bad karma (las 'action, karma' + ngan 'bad')
glossary.ལཱ་སྱ་མ: lā sya ma — Lāsyā, 'she of the dance' (lā sya, Sanskrit lāsya 'dance', in Tibetan letters, + -ma, feminine): a female bodhisattva
glossary.ལོངས་སྤྱོད་རྫོགས་པའི་སྐུ་རུ: longs spyod rdzogs pa'i sku ru — as the body of perfect enjoyment (longs spyod rdzogs pa'i sku 'body of perfect enjoyment', the radiant form in which a buddha appears in visions, + -ru 'as')
glossary.ལོངས་སྤྱོད་རྫོགས་པའི་སྐུར: longs spyod rdzogs pa'i skur — as the body of perfect enjoyment (longs spyod rdzogs pa'i sku + -r 'as')
glossary.ལྕགས་ཀྱུ: lcags kyu — iron hook (lcags 'iron' + kyu 'hook'): the hook by which the light of compassion draws one out
glossary.ལྟ་བར: lta bar — in looking, looking (lta 'look' + -bar): mig ma lta bar 'without looking with the eye'
glossary.ལྟ་བུའི: lta bu'i — like, of the kind of (lta bu 'like' + -'i): me long lta bu'i 'like a mirror'
glossary.ལྡན་པ: ldan pa — having, endowed with (ldan 'have, possess' + -pa)
glossary.ལྡན་པའི: ldan pa'i — of the endowed, endowed with (ldan pa 'having' + -'i 'of'): dpal dang ldan pa'i 'endowed with glory'
glossary.ལྷ་ཚོགས: lha tshogs — host of deities (lha 'god' + tshogs 'host, gathering')
glossary.ཤིང: shing — and, while (links two verbs; also cing, zhing)
glossary.ཤེས: shes — to know, to recognise (shes); ngo shes 'recognise, know the face'
glossary.ཤེས་བར: shes bar — to know, to recognise (shes 'know' + -bar, to); the print's spelling of shes par
glossary.ས: sa — ground, earth; the earth element (sa)
glossary.ས་རུ: sa ru — to the level, to the stage (sa 'ground, level' + -ru 'to'): the stage a buddha has reached
glossary.སངས་རྒྱས་པར: sangs rgyas par — to being a buddha, as a buddha (sangs rgyas 'buddha' + -pa + -r 'to'): sangs rgyas par 'gyur 'become a buddha'
glossary.སངས་རྒྱས་སྤྱན་མ: sangs rgyas spyan ma — Buddha-Eye (sangs rgyas 'buddha' + spyan 'eye, respectful' + -ma, feminine; Sanskrit Buddhalocanā): the consort of the east
glossary.སངས་རྒྱས་སྤྱན་མས: sangs rgyas spyan mas — by Buddha-Eye, by Buddhalocanā (sangs rgyas spyan ma + -s 'by')
glossary.སའི་སྙིང་པོ: sa'i snying po — Essence of the Earth (sa 'earth' + -'i + snying po 'essence'; Sanskrit Kṣitigarbha): a bodhisattva
glossary.སེམས་མ: sems ma — female bodhisattva (sems ma, short for sems dpa' ma)
glossary.སྐུ་མདོག: sku mdog — body colour, colour of a buddha or deity (sku 'body' + mdog 'colour'), the respectful word
glossary.སྐྱབས་སུ: skyabs su — for refuge, as refuge (skyabs 'refuge' + -su 'to'): skyabs su mchi'o 'I go for refuge'
glossary.སྐྱེས: skyes — arisen, born (skyes, past of skye 'be born, arise')
glossary.སྐྱོར: skyor — to hold up, to support (skyor, the present stem, which also serves as the imperative 'hold up!'; past and future bskyor)
glossary.སྐྱོལ: skyol — bring! deliver! (skyol, imperative of skyel 'to bring, to convey')
glossary.སྐྲག: skrag — to be frightened, to be terrified (skrag); fright
glossary.སྐྲག་པ: skrag pa — fright, being frightened (skrag 'be frightened' + -pa)
glossary.སྙམ་བའི: snyam ba'i — of thinking (snyam 'think' + -ba'i, the print's spelling of -pa'i 'of')
glossary.སྙིང: snying — heart (snying); snying mi dga' 'the heart not glad', sad
glossary.སྙིང་ཁར: snying khar — at the heart, into the heart (snying kha 'heart' + -r 'at, into')
glossary.སྟུག་པོ་བཀོད་པའི: stug po bkod pa'i — of the Densely Arrayed (stug po 'thick, dense' + bkod pa 'arranged, set out', bkod past of 'god + -'i 'of'; Sanskrit Ghanavyūha): the name of a buddha-field, in this book that of the centre
glossary.སྟེ: ste — and, namely: a linking word after a verb or a statement, leading on to what follows (also te, de)
glossary.སྡིག་སྒྲིབ: sdig sgrib — sinful obscuration, the veil that harmful deeds leave on the mind (sdig 'sin' + sgrib 'obscuration')
glossary.སྤོངས་ཤིག: spongs shig — give up! (spongs, imperative of spong 'give up', + shig, which marks a command)
glossary.སྨོན་ལམ: smon lam — prayer of aspiration (smon 'to wish' + lam 'path')
glossary.སྲན: sran — endurance, the power to endure (sran)

about: This part finishes the first day and tells the second and the third. The reader warns the dead man not to be drawn to the dull white light of the gods, the path of his own delusion, and gives him a prayer to Vairocana to say after him; if he says it with devotion, he dissolves as rainbow light into Vairocana's heart and becomes a buddha in the central realm. If anger and sin make him afraid of the lights, the second day comes: the element water dawns as a white light, and from the eastern realm of Manifest Joy the blue Vajrasattva Akṣobhya appears on an elephant throne, in union with his consort and surrounded by two bodhisattvas and two female bodhisattvas. From his heart the white mirror-like wisdom pierces toward the dead man, and beside it the dull smoky light of hell. He is to trust the bright light, give up his anger and pray to Vajrasattva in the same words. Some, heavy with pride and sin, are afraid even of the hook of this light and flee, and on the third day the element earth dawns as a yellow light: Ratnasambhava comes from the southern realm on a horse throne with his retinue, and his yellow wisdom of sameness comes together with the dull blue light of humans. The part ends with the other way out: if the dead man recognises the light as the radiance of his own awareness, he becomes a buddha without prayer or devotion.
